newsitem.title: UK: NWE straight-run fuel off as refiner dumps product.
newsitem.headline: NWE straight-run fuel off as refiner dumps product.

text.p: NWE straight-run fuel oil prices slid after a northern refinery jettisoned product to free up storage, the second facility to do so this week, traders said on Friday.
The Scandinavian refinery sold some 50,000 tonnes of low sulphur straight-run to a U.S. buyer on Thursday for a price heard to be just above $100 fob.

The deal followed a Wednesday trade of 30,000 tonnes, heard to be at $114 cif, which was also pushed through because of problems with tank space. The material was bound for the French Mediterrranean coast.
Trans-atlantic bids were heard on Friday at $100-$101 fob but no trades were heard done, with big sellers' next cargoes not ready until early April.
European refineries pursued high sulphur Russian material, which was said to be tight in the prompt period.
A cargo of E-4 was bought by a European refiner to load next week on terms that were undisclosed.
Offers of M-40 were heard at three means minus $2. E-4 with a high water content was heard at three means +$4.
